ai.description: *Varanus bengalensis* grows up to 1.75 meters. It is olive-brown with dark spots and a pale, barred belly. Key features include a rounded tail and nostrils positioned closer to the eyes than the snout.
ai.identificationRemarks: The most reliable cue is the nostril shape: *Varanus bengalensis* has oblique, slit-like nostrils located closer to the eyes than the snout tip, unlike other Indian monitors.
ai.habitat: The Bengal monitor inhabits diverse environments, ranging from arid scrublands and tropical forests to agricultural areas, typically from sea level up to 1,500 meters.
ai.behavior: The Bengal monitor is a diurnal predator that uses a flicking, forked tongue to track prey, often climbing trees or digging into burrows to secure its next meal.
ai.reproductionNotes: The Bengal monitor is oviparous, laying a single annual clutch of 8–30 eggs in burrows or termite mounds. Breeding typically occurs from May to July in India.
ai.distributionRemarks: The Bengal monitor is widely distributed across the Indian subcontinent, ranging from sea level to 2,000 meters in diverse habitats including forests and scrublands.
